items.label: section_header
items.text: KEY POINT

items.label: text
items.text: You always have to use the chemical equation to determine which substance is in excess. If we had been given 0.2 mol Mg and 0.3 mol HCl in this reaction it would look like the HCl is in excess because there is more of it. But if you look at the chemical equation you can see that 0.3 mol HCl only reacts with 0.15 mol Mg so there is still not enough HCl to react with all the Mg, so the Mg is still in excess.

items.label: section_header
items.text: KEY POINT

items.label: text
items.text: A reagent is just something that reacts.

items.label: text
items.text: We might be tempted to say that 0.2 mol Mg produces 0.2 mol H2(g) and the mass of H2 = 0.2 × 2 = 0.4 g. Unfortunately this is not the correct answer!

items.label: text
items.text: We can understand why it is not correct by looking at the chemical equation. 1 mol Mg reacts with 2 mol HCl and therefore 0.2 mol Mg would react with 2 × 0.2 = 0.4 mol HCl.

items.label: text
items.text: But we only used 0.2 mol HCl and so we did not have enough to react with all the Mg. Because all the Mg did not react we cannot use the number of moles of Mg to work out how much hydrogen is produced.

items.label: text
items.text: If we try starting with the number of moles of HCl, we can deduce from the chemical equation that 2 mol HCl reacts with 1 mol Mg, therefore 0.2 mol HCl reacts with 0.1 mol Mg. We added 0.2 mol Mg and so there is more than enough to react with all the HCl- the Mgis in excess.

items.label: text
items.text: Because we know that all the HCl reacts we can use the number of moles of HCl to work out how much H2 is produced.

items.label: text
items.text: 2 mol HCl produce 1 mol H2: the number of moles of H2 is half the number of moles of HCl.

items.label: text
items.text: Therefore 0.2 mol HCl produce 0.1 mol H2.

items.label: text
items.text: The mass of H2 = 0.1 × 2 = 0.2 g.

items.label: text
items.text: This is the correct answer!

items.label: text
items.text: To deduce which substance is in excess we try both numbers of moles in the chemical equation and compare the numbers.

items.label: section_header
items.text: EXAMPLE 8

items.label: text
items.text: Copper reacts with concentrated nitric acid according to the equation:

items.label: formula
items.text: C u ( s ) + 4 H N O _ { 3 } ( a q ) \rightarrow C u ( N O _ { 3 / 2 } ( a q ) + 2 H _ { 2 } O ( I ) + 2 N O _ { 2 } ( g )

items.label: text
items.text: 3.2g of copper is reacted with 0.40 mol concentrated nitric acid. Work out which reagent is in excess.

items.label: text
items.text: We need to convert the mass of Cu to a number of moles:

items.label: formula
items.text: b n u r \, o f \, m o l \, \varsigma \, = \, 0 . 0 5 0 \, m o l

items.label: text
items.text: Looking at the chemical equation we can see that 1 mol Cu reacts with 4 mol HNO3, so we can calculate that:

items.label: text
items.text: 0.050 mol Cu reacts with 4 × 0.050 = 0.20 mol HNO₃

items.label: text
items.text: We have more than 0.20 mol HNO₃ therefore HNO₃ is in excess.

items.label: text
items.text: If the question went further and asked us to calculate the amount in moles of NO2 produced using these quantities we would have to use the number of moles of Cu because not all the HNO₃ is used up. We would obtain 2 × 0.050 = 0.10mol NO2.
